scenario: 你在 AI 编码面试里已经看完代码库、理清了架构和现有接口，还没打开 AI 聊天窗口。
scenario_en: In an AI coding interview, you have already read the codebase, understood the architecture and existing interfaces, and have not opened the AI chat yet.
q: 打开 AI 聊天前，你最应该先做完什么？
q_en: Before opening the AI chat, what should you finish first?
options: 跳过和面试官同步，直接开始写提示
让 AI 先把整个项目重构一遍
形成自己的实现计划，明确关键决策
把原始题目一字不改地粘给 AI
options_en: Skip syncing with the interviewer and jump straight to prompting.
Have the AI refactor the whole project first.
Form your own implementation plan and pin down the key decisions.
Paste the raw problem statement to the AI unchanged.
why: 计划让你掌握架构和算法决策，AI 只是执行者；没有计划就容易被模型的第一版输出牵着走。
why_en: Forming your own plan first keeps architecture and algorithm decisions in your hands instead of the AI's first draft.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Orient[Orientation] --> Plan[Own plan]
  Plan --> Share[Share with interviewer]
  Share --> Prompt[Guide AI]
  Prompt --> Execute[Execute steps]
optionExplanations: 跳过同步只是省了确认步骤，你手上依旧没有成型的实现计划。
把重构交给 AI，它的第一版结构就变成事实架构，关键决策没经过你手。
先想清楚要怎么做、决策点在哪，AI 才有明确目标可以执行。
原样转发题目等于把拆解问题的机会让给 AI，你自己没做任何转译。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping the sync only skips confirmation — you still haven't formed a plan of your own.
Handing the redesign to the AI turns its first draft into the real architecture, with no decision passing through you.
Nail down what you're doing and where the key decisions sit, so the AI has a clear target to execute.
Forwarding the raw prompt hands the job of breaking the problem down to the AI instead of you.

scenario: 你要在动手写代码前先把实现方案定下来，具体怎么定要看面试官对 AI 参与设计的态度。
scenario_en: Before coding, you need to settle the implementation plan, and the right way depends on how the interviewer wants AI involved in design.
q: AI 编码面试里，形成实现计划主要有哪两种方式？
q_en: In an AI coding interview, what are the two main ways to form an implementation plan?
options: 只让 AI 出计划，你全盘接受不追问
完全不做计划，边想边写
只写测试用例，不管架构
自己先设计架构，或者审阅并修改 AI 出的计划
options_en: Let the AI produce a plan and accept it fully without questioning it.
Skip planning entirely and improvise as you go.
Only write test cases and ignore the architecture.
Either design the architecture yourself, or vet and revise a plan the AI drafts.
why: 两种方式都成立：能不能用 AI 参与设计取决于面试官；无论哪种，你都要真正理解并能防守这份计划。
why_en: Either you design the architecture yourself or you vet and revise an AI-drafted plan, but you must understand and defend whichever plan you end up with.
tradeoff: 自己设计架构（慢但可控）vs AI 起草后你审阅（快但要能拆穿它）
optionExplanations: 全盘接受 AI 的计划等于放弃审查，面试官一追问原因你就答不上来。
边想边写等于没有前置计划，一旦题目涉及架构决策就容易走偏。
只盯着测试用例会把架构判断搁置一边，事后返工成本更高。
不管起草者是谁，最终计划都要经你手定稿，你要能讲清每个决策的理由。
optionExplanations_en: Accepting the AI's plan wholesale means giving up review, and you can't answer when the interviewer asks why.
Improvising with no upfront plan leaves you adrift the moment the problem has real architecture decisions.
Focusing only on test cases pushes architecture judgment aside, which costs more to fix later.
Whoever drafts it, the final plan has to pass through you, and you need to be able to explain every decision.

scenario: 面试官明确表示可以用 AI 做设计讨论，你需要快速形成实现路线。
scenario_en: The interviewer explicitly allows AI-assisted design discussion, and you need to form an implementation route quickly.
q: 此时最合适的规划方式是什么？
q_en: What planning mode fits best here?
options: 让 AI 提计划，但逐项审阅、反驳、修改后再执行
直接照 AI 计划做，不追问也不改
拒绝任何 AI 帮助，全部自己手写设计
跳过计划，先让 AI 随便写一版看效果
options_en: Have the AI draft a plan, then review, push back on, and revise it item by item before executing.
Take the AI's plan as-is without questioning or changing anything.
Refuse any AI help and hand-design everything yourself.
Skip planning and let the AI write a random first pass to see what happens.
why: 面试官已经接受 AI 参与设计，AI 辅助规划能加速；但强信号来自你审查和塑形计划，而不是盖章批准。
why_en: Since the interviewer is fine with AI-assisted design, let the AI draft fast, but the strong signal comes from you actively vetting and reshaping the plan.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官希望看你亲自设计，应先自己画出结构，再把 AI 用在实现体力活上。
tradeoff: AI 起草求快 vs 你亲自把关求可控
optionExplanations: 面试官已经放行 AI 参与设计，就让它先起草求快，但每一项都要你审、你改。
原样照做等于把设计判断交给 AI，即使这轮允许用 AI，你也没留下把关痕迹。
本题面试官已经开放 AI 参与，还坚持全手写等于白白放弃这轮明确允许的加速方式。
没有先成型的计划直接摸索，AI 第一版会隐性定型架构，你事后很难说清楚为什么这样设计。
optionExplanations_en: Since the interviewer already opened the door to AI-assisted design, let it draft fast — you still review and revise every piece.
Taking the draft as-is hands the design call to the AI, and there's no sign of your judgment even though review was allowed.
Refusing all AI help here throws away speed the interviewer explicitly said you could use.
Skipping a plan and letting the AI free-write first quietly locks in the architecture, and you'll struggle to explain it later.

scenario: 你不确定这轮面试是否允许 AI 帮你做计划，还是只希望 AI 写实现。
scenario_en: You are not sure whether this interview allows AI to help with planning, or only expects AI to write implementation code.
q: 最好的处理方式是什么？
q_en: What is the best way to handle this?
options: 直接假设可以用 AI 做所有设计
先问面试官对 AI 参与规划的期望
完全不用 AI，全程手写
先按自己的想法做，等面试官发现问题再解释
options_en: Just assume AI can be used for all the design work.
Ask the interviewer up front what they expect from AI in planning.
Avoid AI entirely and write everything by hand.
Do it your own way and explain only if the interviewer objects.
why: 不同公司甚至不同面试官的预期不同，提前对齐能避免把可接受的用法误判成负面信号。
why_en: Ask the interviewer directly, because expectations for AI in planning vary by company and by interviewer.
whenOtherWins: 如果规则已经在题面里写清楚，就按规则执行并简短复述你的理解即可，不必再问。
tradeoff: 先问清楚 vs 自行假设后再纠偏
optionExplanations: 凭自己猜测替面试官做了决定，一旦猜错就等于在不该用 AI 设计时用了。
边界不清时先开口确认，一句话就能把后续所有 AI 用法钉死在正确范围内。
全程手写可能白白放弃面试官本来允许的加速手段，规则还没确认就先自我设限。
先斩后奏、等被指出才补救，既被动又显得你事先没想清楚边界。
optionExplanations_en: Guessing on the interviewer's behalf means you might use AI for design exactly when you weren't supposed to.
When the boundary is unclear, one quick question locks down how you can use AI for the rest of the round.
Going fully hand-written can throw away speed the interviewer would have allowed, based on a rule you never confirmed.
Doing it your way and explaining only when caught is reactive, and signals you never thought about the boundary upfront.

q: 补全 AI 规划的分界线：
q_en: Fill in the boundary line for AI-assisted planning:
text: 理解后提出反驳和修改叫{{审阅计划}}；看不懂却点头照做叫{{橡皮图章}}。
why: 面试官看的是你是否还在控制方案：理解后提出反驳和修改是审阅计划；看不懂却点头照做是橡皮图章。
why_en: The line is vetting versus rubber-stamping: pushing back on a plan you understand is control, nodding along to one you couldn't have written is not.
tradeoff: 审阅计划（理解+修改，慢但可控）vs 橡皮图章（照单全收，快但空心）

termDefinitions.meaning: 看不懂却直接盖章通过的行为，这里指对 AI 计划不加判断就照做。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rubber-stamping means approving something without understanding it, here nodding along to an AI plan you couldn't defend.

scenario: 45 分钟的题面写着：先修 parser bug，再加搜索功能，最后优化性能。
scenario_en: Your 45-minute problem statement says: fix the parser bug, then add search, then optimize performance.
q: 多数 AI 编码面试题为什么需要先拆分阶段？
q_en: Why do most AI coding interview problems need to be split into phases first?
options: 因为 AI 每次只能生成一行代码
因为拆分能让你跳过写测试这一步
因为问题常含修 bug、加功能、优化等多阶段
因为这类题目从来没有现成代码库
options_en: Because the AI can only generate one line of code at a time.
Because decomposition lets you skip writing tests.
Because these problems usually bundle multiple phases like fixing a bug, adding a feature, then optimizing.
Because this kind of problem never starts with an existing codebase.
why: 多阶段题需要你判断顺序和依赖，否则 AI 容易一次性生成难以验证的大块代码。
why_en: Multi-phase problems need you to decide the order and dependencies, or the AI will produce one large, hard-to-verify block of code.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  BigTask[Big task] --> Phase1[Baseline]
  BigTask --> Phase2[Core feature]
  BigTask --> Phase3[Edges]
  Phase1 --> Prompt1[Small prompt]
  Phase2 --> Prompt2[Small prompt]
optionExplanations: 这个说法不成立，AI 完全能一次输出大段代码，限制不在这里。
拆分和是否写测试无关，每个阶段该测的部分照样要测。
阶段之间彼此有顺序和依赖，你得先想清楚顺序再分步提示 AI。
很多这类面试其实带现成代码库，这不是要拆分的理由。
optionExplanations_en: That's not actually true — the AI can output a large block in one go, so that's not the real limit.
Splitting the work has nothing to do with skipping tests; each phase still needs its own checks.
The phases depend on each other in order, so you have to work out that order before prompting step by step.
Plenty of these interviews do start from an existing codebase, so that's not the real reason to decompose.

scenario: 类似 Shopify 的开放式题：空仓库加一份 README，60 分钟内要交出能跑的小应用。
scenario_en: A Shopify-style open-ended round: an empty repo and a README, with a working small app due in 60 minutes.
q: 开放式从零构建时，哪些顺序原则通常成立？（多选）
q_en: For open-ended greenfield builds, which ordering principles usually hold? (Select all)
options: 先建数据模型，再写依赖这些模型的逻辑
先做核心功能，再补边界情况
先修会影响后续功能的 bug，再加依赖它的新功能
先优化还不存在的代码
options_en: Model your data first, then write the logic that depends on it.
Build the core functionality before handling edge cases.
Fix bugs that block later features before adding features that depend on them.
Optimize code that doesn't exist yet.
why: 这三条顺序能减少返工；反过来先优化还没成形的代码，往往把复杂度引到错误的地方。
why_en: Model-first, core-before-edge, and fix-before-feature ordering reduce rework, while optimizing code that doesn't exist yet wastes effort.
optionExplanations: 先定好对象和关系，后续逻辑才有稳定边界可以依靠。
主路径先跑通，剩下的少数分支能逐个补，不拖累主线。
先解除卡住后续功能的坏基础，别在它上面继续叠新功能。
代码还没写出来，根本没有可测的东西能拿来调优。
optionExplanations_en: Nail down the objects and relations first, so later logic has a stable boundary to build on.
Get the main path working first, then the few edge branches can be patched in without derailing it.
Clear the blocking bug before stacking a new feature on top of a broken base.
There's no code yet to profile or tune — there's nothing to optimize.

scenario: 类似 Shopify 的开放式教程题：你从空仓库和 README 开始，要构建一个小应用。
scenario_en: In a Shopify-like open-ended tutorial task, you start from an empty repo and a README and need to build a small app.
q: 最先应该让计划解决什么？
q_en: What should your plan solve first?
options: 最终性能优化
UI 配色
让 AI 一次写完整应用
先定义核心实体和数据结构
options_en: Final performance optimization.
The UI color scheme.
Let the AI write the entire app in one shot.
Define the core entities and data structures first.
why: 数据结构先定下来，会迫使你先理解系统对象和关系，后续逻辑才有稳定边界。
why_en: Modeling entities first in greenfield work forces you to understand the system's objects and relationships before any logic is written.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目是已有代码里的单点 bug，先定位失败路径比重新建模更重要。
tradeoff: 先建数据模型求稳定边界 vs 先让 AI 快速出一版看效果
optionExplanations: 系统结构还没成形就调优，之后架构一变这些优化全部作废。
配色不影响核心逻辑对不对，不该抢在架构判断前面处理。
把整个应用交给 AI 一次写完，你之后很难解释每个类的职责为什么这样分。
空仓库起步先把对象和关系定下来，后面每一步逻辑才有依据。
optionExplanations_en: Tuning performance before the structure even exists means the work gets thrown away once the architecture shifts.
Color choices don't affect whether the core logic is correct, so they shouldn't jump ahead of the architecture call.
Letting the AI write the whole app in one shot leaves you unable to explain why each class has the responsibilities it does.
Starting from an empty repo, pin down the objects and their relations first so every later step has something to build on.

scenario: 你直接对 AI 说“build the whole task scheduler”，指望它一次产出全部实现。
scenario_en: You just tell the AI to build the whole task scheduler and expect the entire implementation in one shot.
q: 缺少拆分时，AI 最容易生成什么样的代码？
q_en: Without decomposition, what kind of code is the AI most likely to generate?
options: 清晰、可验证、每步可解释的小改动
职责太杂的大块代码，需求一变就难重构
完全不包含任何实现
只包含测试
options_en: Clean, verifiable, small changes you can explain step by step.
One large block of code that covers too many responsibilities and is hard to refactor once requirements shift.
No implementation at all.
Only test code.
why: 大而泛的提示会把多个决策埋进一个输出，直到很晚才暴露错误方向。
why_en: A broad, undecomposed prompt buries many decisions inside one output, so a wrong direction only surfaces very late.
optionExplanations: 这是拆分得当时才会出现的结果，不是本题问的缺少拆分的后果。
职责混在一起，需求一变就要大改，返工成本随之升高。
AI 通常会给出实现，完全不产出代码不是常见的规划风险。
只有测试没有实现，没法验证真实行为，也不是缺少拆分的典型后果。
optionExplanations_en: That's what good decomposition produces — not the outcome of skipping it, which is what's being asked here.
Responsibilities get tangled together, so any requirement change forces a big rewrite and heavier rework.
The AI usually does produce an implementation; producing nothing at all isn't the typical risk here.
Tests with no implementation can't verify real behavior, and that's not the typical fallout from skipping decomposition either.

scenario: 你在给一个任务调度器写提示，手上这两条候选提示要判断粒度是否合适。
scenario_en: You're sizing prompts for a task scheduler and have to judge whether these two candidates hit the right granularity.
q: “Build the scheduler”和“Write the Task constructor”分别错在哪里？
q_en: What is wrong with “Build the scheduler” versus “Write the Task constructor”?
options: 前者太宽，后者太窄
前者太窄，后者太宽
两者都是理想粒度
两者都不能给 AI
options_en: "Build the scheduler" is too broad, and "Write the Task constructor" is too narrow.
"Build the scheduler" is too narrow, and "Write the Task constructor" is too broad.
Both prompts are the ideal granularity.
Neither prompt should ever be given to the AI.
why: 前者把多个算法和设计决策混在一个提示里；后者只是你自己可以直接手写的一行级任务。
why_en: The broad prompt bundles several algorithm and design decisions into one shot, while the narrow one is just a single line you'd type yourself.
tradeoff: 提示太宽（AI 决策过多，难验证）vs 提示太窄（你在替 AI 打字，没有价值）
codeSample:
太宽: "Build the scheduler"
太窄: "Write the Task constructor"
右粒度: 建 Task/Dependency 类型 -> 建依赖图 -> 拓扑排序 -> 处理 cycle
optionExplanations: 校准提示粒度正好卡在两者之间：一个太宽把决策全扔给 AI，一个太窄等于替它打字。
方向说反了：Build the scheduler 才是那个过宽的提示，不是过窄。
两个例子分别踩了过宽和过窄两个极端，都不是理想粒度。
两个提示都能用，只是各自需要往中间粒度调整，不是完全不能给 AI。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the calibration point in the middle: one prompt hands over every decision, the other has you typing for the AI.
The direction is flipped — "Build the scheduler" is the broad one, not the narrow one.
Each example sits at an opposite extreme, so neither is the ideal granularity.
Both prompts are usable, they just need to shift toward the middle granularity — neither is off-limits to the AI.

q: 把 task scheduler with dependencies 的合理拆分排好：
q_en: Put the reasonable decomposition for a task scheduler with dependencies in order:
steps: 用拓扑排序计算合法执行顺序
建 Task 和 Dependency 类型
why: 先建 Task/Dependency 模型，把输入转成依赖图，再用拓扑排序求执行顺序，最后单独处理无解的 cycle。
why_en: For dependency scheduling: model tasks first, build the graph, topologically sort it, then handle the cycle case separately.
tradeoff: 一次性大提示（AI 承担全部决策）vs 按拓扑顺序拆成 4 个小步骤（你逐步验证）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Model[Model tasks] --> Graph[Build dependency graph]
  Graph --> Ready[Find ready tasks]
  Ready --> Schedule[Assign workers]
  Schedule --> Verify[Verify order]

termDefinitions.meaning: 对有向无环图的节点排序，使每个节点排在它依赖的节点之后。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort orders the nodes of a directed acyclic graph so each node comes after everything it depends on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 依赖图里出现环状依赖，导致不存在合法执行顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cycle is a circular dependency in the graph, which means no valid execution order exists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 任务之间的先后依赖关系，通常建模成图中的一条有向边。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dependency is a must-come-before relationship between tasks, usually modeled as a directed edge in the graph.

scenario: 面试时长 45-60 分钟，你要把整道题拆成几个主要阶段写进计划里。
scenario_en: In a 45 to 60 minute interview, you need to split the whole problem into a few main phases in your plan.
q: 这道题的计划粒度，拆成几个阶段最匹配这个时长？
q_en: For that interview length, how many phases is the right planning granularity?
options: 只给一个笼统步骤，让 AI 自己规划全部实现
拆成三到五个可独立验证的阶段
拆成十几个逐行级别的小步骤
步骤数量不设上限，越细越好
options_en: Give the AI one vague step and let it plan the entire implementation.
Break it into three to five independently verifiable phases.
Break it into a dozen-plus line-by-line micro-steps.
Don't cap the step count at all — finer is always better.
why: 45-60 分钟 ÷ 一步一次提示-验证周期 ≈ 3-5 步；这个数字决定你该把计划切多细，也是后面判断有没有过度拆分的参照。
why_en: Divide the 45 to 60 minute interview by one prompt-and-verify cycle per step and you land on three to five steps, which sets how finely to slice your plan.
optionExplanations: 一步到底等于把全部架构决策交给 AI，45-60 分钟根本来不及逐项验证。
把 45 到 60 分钟按单步提示加验证来分配，落点刚好是三到五步。
十几个逐行步骤远超这个时长能验证的次数，变成人工盯着 AI 打字。
步骤越细耗时越多，超出面试时长就没时间跑完整个实现。
optionExplanations_en: One catch-all step hands the AI every architecture call, and 45 to 60 minutes isn't enough to verify it piece by piece.
Pace it at one prompt-and-verify cycle per step across 45 to 60 minutes and you land on three to five steps.
A dozen-plus line-by-line steps blows past how many checks that time budget can fit, turning into micromanaging.
The finer you slice it the more time it eats, and you'll run out of interview time before finishing the build.

scenario: 你已经形成计划：先修 parser bug，再用 BFS 加搜索功能，最后若需要处理加权边再优化。
scenario_en: You have a plan: fix the parser bug first, add search with BFS, then optimize for weighted edges if needed.
q: 在提示 AI 前应该做什么？
q_en: What should you do before prompting the AI?
options: 只在心里记住，不说出来
直接把三步一次性丢给 AI
把计划告诉面试官，给他们纠偏窗口
先优化再修 bug
options_en: Keep it in your head and never say it out loud.
Dump all three steps on the AI in one prompt.
Say the plan out loud to the interviewer so they get a chance to redirect you.
Optimize first, then fix the bug.
why: 说出计划展示战略思考，也给面试官一个在你走偏前就能提醒你的窗口。
why_en: Stating your plan out loud shows strategic thinking and gives the interviewer a window to redirect you before you head the wrong way.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目极小，也至少用一句话说明当前顺序和理由，而不是完全跳过。
tradeoff: 说出计划（多花十秒，换纠偏机会）vs 直接开始写（更快，但走偏了没人拦）

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按层扩展、常用于求无权图的最短路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, or Breadth-First Search, expands level by level and is commonly used to find shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把输入文本解析成结构化数据的组件，这里指代码里已有的解析模块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A parser is the component that turns raw input text into structured data.

optionExplanations: 计划只留在你脑子里，面试官没有共享上下文，后面每次提示都要重新解释背景。
三步一次性丢给 AI，三个决策被压进一次输出，容易生成难验证的大块代码。
已经形成计划时，先花几秒说给面试官听，能在你走偏前就被拦住。
parser 的 bug 还没修，后面靠它的搜索功能等于建在坏地基上。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping the plan in your head only means the interviewer has no shared context, and you re-explain the background every prompt after.
Dumping all three steps on the AI at once buries three decisions in a single output that's hard to verify.
Once you have a plan, saying it out loud gives the interviewer a few seconds to redirect you before you drift.
The parser bug is still broken, so the search feature you build next sits on a bad foundation.

scenario: 面试官全程看着你的屏幕，你刚定好三阶段计划，还没敲第一个提示。
scenario_en: The interviewer is watching your screen; you've just settled on a three-phase plan and haven't typed the first prompt.
q: 把计划说给面试官听有哪些作用？（多选）
q_en: What does saying your plan out loud to the interviewer accomplish? (Select all)
options: 保证 AI 输出永远正确
展示你在战略性思考
给面试官机会及时纠偏
建立共享上下文，后续提示更容易被理解
options_en: It guarantees the AI's output is always correct.
It shows you're thinking strategically.
It gives the interviewer a chance to redirect you early.
It creates shared context so your later prompts are easier to follow.
why: 计划沟通能同步方向和评估点，但仍需要你在执行时验证 AI 的结果，它不会替你保证正确性。
why_en: Sharing the plan syncs direction and gives the interviewer something to evaluate, but you still have to verify the AI's output yourself.
optionExplanations: 说出计划不能替代验证这一步，AI 仍可能跑偏或出错。
十秒话就能让面试官判断你是不是有方向，而不只是在打字。
面试官能在你投入实现前先拦住走偏的方向，省下返工时间。
后面每个提示，面试官都能对上你当前在做哪一步，少一次重新解释。
optionExplanations_en: Saying the plan out loud doesn't replace verification — the AI can still drift or get it wrong.
Ten seconds of talking lets the interviewer tell you have direction, not just that you're typing.
The interviewer can stop a wrong turn before you sink time implementing it.
Every prompt after that, the interviewer can place which step you're on, so you skip re-explaining.

scenario: 你已经决定在现有 `Grid` 类上用 BFS 找迷宫最短路径。
scenario_en: You have decided to use BFS on the existing `Grid` class to find the shortest maze path.
q: 哪条提示最能体现“用计划指导 AI”？
q_en: Which prompt best shows that you are using your plan to guide the AI?
options: 跟 AI 说 solve the maze 就行，别的不用管
在 Grid 类里用 BFS，指定入口和返回坐标路径
随便写个高效算法，思路交给 AI 决定
先把 Grid 类整个重写一遍再说
options_en: "Just tell the AI to solve the maze, nothing else specified."
"Implement BFS in the Grid class, with a named entry point and a returned coordinate path."
"Write some efficient algorithm, leave the approach up to the AI."
"Rewrite the whole Grid class first."
why: 提示把算法选择、入口对象和返回值都交代清楚，AI 负责实现细节，而不是替你决定路线。
why_en: This prompt spells out the chosen algorithm, the entry object, and the return value, so the AI implements your plan instead of choosing its own route.
whenOtherWins: 如果边权不一致，BFS 不再适合最短路径，应改用 Dijkstra 或 A*，并在提示里说明原因。
codeSample:
Implement BFS in the existing Grid class.
Start from start, stop at end, and return the shortest path as a list of coordinates.
Use the existing Cell representation; do not introduce a parallel grid model.
tradeoff: 笼统提示（AI 决定算法，快但失控）vs 精确提示（你决定算法，AI 负责落地）
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Raw[Raw prompt] --> AI[AI chooses plan]
  AI --> Drift[Drift]

flowchart LR
  Plan[Plan] --> AI[Focused implementation]
  AI --> Review[Review diff]

flowchart LR
  Vague[Vague ask] --> AI[AI guesses structure]
  AI --> Mismatch[Mismatch risk]

flowchart LR
  Rewrite[Rewrite all] --> Scope[Scope creep]
  Scope --> Risk[Risk]

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按层扩展节点，能在无权图里找到最短路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands nodes level by level and finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理带权最短路径的经典算法，权重非负时保证最优解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths in weighted graphs and guarantees optimality when weights are non-negative.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 Dijkstra 基础上加启发函数、更快收敛到目标的最短路径算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A-star adds a heuristic on top of Dijkstra's algorithm to reach the target faster.

optionExplanations: 只说 solve the maze，AI 会自己挑算法和结构，你的判断没有出现在提示里。
算法、入口对象、返回格式都写清楚了，AI 复用现有 Cell，产出能直接接进代码库。
只要求高效不指定算法，AI 可能选一个和现有 Grid/Cell 不兼容的实现。
没必要的重写会把范围扩大到 Grid 本身，偏离找最短路径这个目标。
optionExplanations_en: Just saying "solve the maze" lets the AI pick its own algorithm and structure — your judgment never makes it into the prompt.
Naming the algorithm, entry point, and return format means the AI reuses the existing Cell and the result drops straight into the codebase.
Asking only for efficiency without naming an algorithm risks the AI picking something incompatible with the existing Grid and Cell.
An unnecessary rewrite drags scope onto the Grid class itself, away from the actual goal of finding the shortest path.

scenario: 题面是一段英文需求，代码库已有既定接口风格，你想省时间整段粘给 AI。
scenario_en: The problem is an English spec, the codebase already has its own interface conventions, and you want to save time by pasting it straight into the AI.
q: 把原始题目直接粘给 AI，而不先转化成自己的计划，主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of pasting the raw problem into AI instead of translating it into your own plan first?
options: AI 一定无法理解英文题目
代码会自动通过全部测试
你会因此节省验证时间
AI 给方案，但未必贴合代码库或预期
options_en: The AI definitely can't understand an English problem statement.
The code will automatically pass all the tests.
You'll end up saving time on verification.
The AI will produce a solution, but it might not fit the codebase or expectations.
why: 原题提示让模型自己决定关键路线，你也失去了展示问题拆解和选型判断的机会。
why_en: Pasting the raw problem lets the model pick the approach on its own, and you lose the chance to show your own decomposition and judgment.
optionExplanations: 现代模型理解英文题目基本没有障碍，这不是真实风险。
方案通不通过测试，跟有没有先转化成自己的计划没有必然关系。
跳过转化通常不会省验证时间，返工反而可能更多。
AI 会给出方案，但它自己选的路线可能忽略代码库结构或面试官的期待。
optionExplanations_en: Modern models have no real trouble reading an English prompt — that's not the actual risk.
Whether the code passes the tests has no direct link to whether you translated the problem into your own plan.
Skipping the translation step rarely saves verification time — it usually means more rework instead.
The AI will produce something, but the route it picks on its own can ignore the codebase's structure or what's expected.

q: 补全好提示应包含的上下文：
q_en: Fill in the context a good prompt should include:
text: 好的实现提示应说明选择的{{算法}}、要复用的{{数据结构}}，以及如何和现有{{接口}}交互。
why: 这些信息让 AI 沿你的计划写代码，而不是发明并行架构；缺一项，AI 就多一分自由决定权。
why_en: A good implementation prompt names the algorithm, the data structures to reuse, and the existing interfaces so the AI follows your plan instead of inventing its own.

scenario: 你已经想清楚要用 BFS，却在提示里逐行写出变量名、循环结构和每句代码。
scenario_en: You've already settled on BFS, but your prompt spells out variable names, loop structure, and every single line.
q: 提示“太具体”会带来什么问题？
q_en: What problem does an overly specific prompt create?
options: 你变成逐行口述，AI 只是代打
AI 会掌握太多上下文信息
输出内容一定会变得更短
面试官会看不到你的想法
options_en: You end up dictating line by line, and the AI is just typing for you.
The AI ends up with too much context.
The output is guaranteed to be shorter.
The interviewer can no longer see your thinking.
why: 目标是指导 AI 实现你的方案，而不是把每个变量名和每行代码都口述给它。
why_en: The goal is to direct the AI to implement your approach, not to dictate every variable name and every line yourself.
tradeoff: 太具体（你在打字，AI 只是代打）vs 右粒度（你定方向，AI 处理实现体力活）
optionExplanations: 提示细到每个变量名，你花的时间跟自己打字差不多，AI 没帮你分担设计。
上下文多少不是问题所在，缺的是留给 AI 的判断空间。
输出长短不是核心问题，谁在做设计决策才是关键。
面试官反而能看到你在口述每一行，只是看到的是打字而不是判断。
optionExplanations_en: When the prompt spells out every variable name, you spend as much time as typing it yourself — the AI isn't carrying any design load.
The amount of context isn't the issue — what's missing is room for the AI to actually judge anything.
Output length isn't the core problem — who's making the design call is.
The interviewer actually sees you dictating every line, just typing instead of deciding.

scenario: 你的计划里定了用 BFS 找最短路径，AI 交回来的代码却换成了 Dijkstra。
scenario_en: Your plan called for BFS to find the shortest path, but the code the AI hands back uses Dijkstra instead.
q: AI 回来后偷偷把你选的算法换成另一个，应该怎么处理？
q_en: If the AI quietly swaps your chosen algorithm for another one, how should you respond?
options: 只要能编译就接受
立即放弃原计划，不解释
看理由站不站得住，站不住就纠偏
忽略测试
options_en: Accept it as long as it compiles.
Abandon your original plan immediately without asking why.
Check whether there's a good reason; if not, correct it and redirect the AI.
Ignore the tests.
why: 模型可以提供替代思路，但方案改变必须经过你判断，否则你就不再是驱动者。
why_en: The model can propose alternatives, but any change of approach must pass through your judgment, or you stop being the one driving.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Output[AI output] --> Drift{Changed algorithm?}
  Drift -->|yes| Stop[Stop and name drift]
  Stop --> Repoint[Repoint prompt]
  Repoint --> Verify[Verify against plan]
optionExplanations: 编译通过只说明语法没问题，不代表换掉的算法真的适合这道题。
不问理由直接放弃计划，如果 AI 的替代方案其实更好，你就白白丢了一个合理 pivot。
先判断替代算法有没有站得住的理由，站得住就用，站不住就纠偏重定向。
跳过测试只会让偷换算法的副作用更晚才暴露出来。
optionExplanations_en: Compiling only means the syntax is fine — it says nothing about whether the swapped algorithm actually fits this problem.
Dropping the plan without asking why means you might be throwing away a genuinely better alternative.
Check whether the swap has a solid reason first — keep it if it does, correct and redirect the AI if it doesn't.
Skipping the tests just delays when the side effects of the swapped algorithm finally show up.

scenario: 面试过半，三阶段计划刚执行到第二阶段，你在判断要不要改计划。
scenario_en: You're halfway through the interview, on phase two of your three-phase plan, weighing whether to revise it.
q: 哪些情况是修改计划的合理理由？（多选）
q_en: Which situations are valid reasons to revise the plan? (Select all)
options: 发现新的性能约束
数据模型比取向时看到的更复杂
AI 随口建议重写一切但你说不出理由
面试官给出改变范围的提示
options_en: You discover a new performance constraint.
The data model turns out more complex than it looked during orientation.
The AI casually suggests rewriting everything and you can't say why that would help.
The interviewer drops a hint that changes the scope.
why: 计划应该随新事实变化，而不是随 AI 的每一个建议摇摆。
why_en: Revise the plan when new facts change the problem, not just because the AI suggests something different.
optionExplanations: 约束一变，原计划可能不再可行，这时候改是有依据的。
模型复杂度变了，原来的拆分粒度和接口边界可能不够用了。
没有收益说明的重写建议只是噪声，跟着走等于把方向让给了 AI。
范围一变，哪些组件还要不要做都会跟着变，计划自然要跟上。
optionExplanations_en: When a constraint changes, the original plan may no longer hold up, so revising it is grounded in fact.
If the model turns out more complex, your original phase sizing and interface boundaries may no longer be enough.
A rewrite suggestion with no stated payoff is just noise — following it hands the direction over to the AI.
A scope change shifts which components still need building, so the plan has to move with it.

scenario: AI 建议用另一种数据结构，你能清楚解释它如何更好满足新发现的约束。
scenario_en: The AI suggests another data structure, and you can clearly explain how it better satisfies a newly discovered constraint.
q: 这属于什么情况？
q_en: What situation is this?
options: 失去控制
合理 pivot
必须拒绝 AI
测试无关紧要
options_en: Losing control of the design.
A legitimate pivot.
Something you must reject outright.
Something where tests no longer matter.
why: 只要新方案的理由来自你对约束的理解，采纳 AI 的建议也算是你在掌控。
why_en: Adopting the AI's suggestion still counts as control as long as you can explain why it better fits the newly discovered constraint.
whenOtherWins: 如果你说不出收益，就先保留原计划，或要求 AI 给出可验证的理由再考虑。
tradeoff: 坚持原计划（一致但可能过时）vs 采纳有理由的建议（灵活但要你能讲清楚为什么）
optionExplanations: 只要理由站得住脚，采纳建议不等于失控，这个说法过于绝对。
你能讲清新数据结构为什么更贴合刚发现的约束，方向依然是你在决定。
一刀切拒绝会让你错过一个真正更合适的方案。
换了数据结构之后更需要测试验证行为没有变化，不是可以忽略。
optionExplanations_en: As long as the reason holds up, taking the suggestion isn't losing control — that call is too absolute.
You can explain exactly why the new structure fits the newly found constraint, so the direction is still yours.
Rejecting every suggestion outright means missing a genuinely better option.
Swapping data structures makes testing more necessary, not less — behavior still needs verifying.

scenario: 你在修一个 parser bug，AI 连续三轮建议换框架、重写类层级，都没说清和这个 bug 的关系。
scenario_en: You're fixing a parser bug, and for three turns straight the AI has pushed framework swaps and class rewrites without tying any of it to the bug.
q: AI 反复建议大重写、换框架、从头再来，却说不清楚道理，这种现象在 AI 编码面试里通常叫什么？
q_en: In an AI coding interview, what is it called when the AI repeatedly suggests big rewrites, framework swaps, or starting over without a clear reason?
options: Scope creep
Rubber-stamping
Test-driven iteration
AI spiral
options_en: Scope creep
Rubber-stamping
Test-driven iteration
An AI spiral
why: 这叫 AI spiral——模型不知道答案时开始乱提大重写建议，需要你停下来重新评估，而不是跟着转。
why_en: This is called an AI spiral: the model flails by proposing rewrites when it doesn't know the answer, and you need to stop and reassess instead of following along.

termDefinitions.meaning: 范围蔓延：改动或需求不断超出原计划边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is when changes or requirements keep expanding beyond the original plan.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不理解却直接照单全收的行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rubber-stamping means approving something without actually understanding it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型没有把握时开始乱提大重写、换框架等建议的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An AI spiral is when the model flails by proposing large rewrites or framework changes because it doesn't actually know the answer.

optionExplanations: Scope creep 描述的是需求或范围不断膨胀，不是模型说不清理由的乱提议。
Rubber-stamping 说的是你照单全收的态度，不是模型本身反复乱建议的行为。
Test-driven iteration 是先写测试再实现的正向流程，跟无根据的大重写无关。
模型没把握时靠乱提大重写制造进展感，这种现象就叫 AI spiral。
optionExplanations_en: Scope creep describes requirements or scope steadily ballooning, not the model flailing with unexplained suggestions.
Rubber-stamping describes your own habit of nodding along, not the model's repeated behavior.
Test-driven iteration is the healthy write-tests-first flow, unrelated to baseless big rewrites.
When the model fakes progress by pitching big rewrites it can't justify, that's called an AI spiral.

scenario: AI 连续建议重构类层级、换框架、从头开始，但没有解释这些如何解决当前 bug。
scenario_en: The AI keeps suggesting class hierarchy refactors, framework swaps, and starting over, but does not explain how any of that fixes the current bug.
q: 最好的反应是什么？
q_en: What is the best response?
options: 停下来重新定位问题，给 AI 更小的任务
跟着重写，保持表面上的“进展”
把测试删掉，避免暴露问题
直接结束这场面试
options_en: Stop, re-pin down the actual problem, and give the AI a smaller, more concrete task.
Go along with the rewrite to keep up the appearance of progress.
Delete the tests so the problem stops showing up.
Just end the interview outright.
why: AI spiral 要靠你主动打断，回到问题本身和可验证的小步骤，而不是跟着模型的大动作走。
why_en: You have to interrupt an AI spiral yourself by reassessing the actual problem and handing the AI a smaller, verifiable task.
whenOtherWins: 如果架构确实阻止了需求实现，也要先讲清证据和最小迁移方案，而不是盲目重写。
tradeoff: 跟着 AI 重写（看似有进展，实则失控）vs 停下重新定位（慢一拍，但保持可验证）
optionExplanations: 先缩小任务范围，你就能重新验证每一步，不被卷入无根据的重写。
重写没解释怎么解决当前 bug，那种进展只是表面的。
删测试只会掩盖问题，bug 本身仍然存在。
结束面试放弃了展示你能识别并处理 AI spiral 的机会。
optionExplanations_en: Shrinking the task first lets you verify each step again instead of getting swept into an unjustified rewrite.
The rewrite never explains how it fixes the current bug, so that progress is only surface-level.
Deleting the tests just hides the problem — the bug is still there.
Ending the interview throws away the chance to show you can spot and handle an AI spiral.

q: 补全高质量 pivot 叙述：
q_en: Complete a high-quality pivot statement:
text: “我发现 brute force 对 phase three 的大输入{{不扩展}}，所以我会切到{{heap-based}}方案。”
why: 这句话把问题、触发约束和新路线一次说清——听起来是适应而不是慌乱，这是高质量 pivot 叙述的模板。
why_en: A strong pivot statement names the scaling problem and the replacement approach in one breath, which reads as adaptation rather than confusion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 穷举所有可能情况的解法，实现简单但通常不能应对大规模输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Brute force means trying every possibility, which is simple to implement but usually does not scale to large inputs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于堆这种数据结构的方案，常用来在大数据量下快速拿到最小/最大元素。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heap-based approach uses a heap data structure to efficiently get the minimum or maximum element even at scale.

q: 把规划到执行的闭环排好：
q_en: Put the planning-to-execution loop in order:
steps: 用第一步计划写具体提示
向面试官说明整体计划
取向后拆成 3-5 个阶段
审阅 AI 输出是否符合该阶段目标
why: 先拆阶段、再向面试官同步计划、然后用当前阶段目标写提示、最后审阅输出是否达标，形成闭环。
why_en: The loop is decompose into phases, state the plan aloud, prompt for the current step, then review the output against that step's goal.
tradeoff: 把整段闭环压成一次性长提示（AI 全权决定）vs 拆成阶段循环，每步都审阅再继续（你逐步把关）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Plan[Plan] --> State[State plan aloud]
  State --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
  Prompt --> Review[Review output]
  Review --> Revise{Need revise?}
  Revise -->|yes| Plan
  Revise -->|no| Next[Next step]

scenario: 平台化的结构化题面已经列好阶段：先修 bug，再加功能，最后优化。
scenario_en: A platform-run structured problem already lists the phases for you: fix the bug, add the feature, then optimize.
q: 结构化面试中，为什么拆分通常比开放式题更明显？
q_en: In a structured interview, why is decomposition usually more obvious than in an open-ended problem?
options: 结构化题没有任何约束
结构化题不需要读代码
因为题面通常已经写明了各阶段顺序
AI 会自动拆成最佳步骤
options_en: Structured problems have no constraints at all.
Structured problems don't require reading any code.
Because the problem statement usually already spells out the phase order.
The AI automatically splits the work into the best steps.
why: 即使阶段已经写明（比如 bug fix -> feature -> optimization），你仍要在每个阶段内判断哪些部分需要自己思考，哪些适合交给 AI 实现。
why_en: Even when phases like bug fix, feature, and optimization are already spelled out, you still decide within each phase how much needs your reasoning versus AI implementation.
optionExplanations: 结构化题通常约束反而更多，比如平台限定的阶段顺序，这个说法不成立。
读懂现有代码仍是每个阶段动手前的前提，不能跳过。
阶段边界题面已经画好，你只需要在每个阶段内继续细化。
AI 不会替你决定阶段内的粒度，拆分的判断始终是你的工作。
optionExplanations_en: Structured problems usually come with more constraints, like a platform-fixed phase order, so that claim doesn't hold.
Reading the existing code is still a prerequisite before touching each phase — you can't skip it.
The phase boundaries are already laid out in the prompt, so you only need to refine within each one.
The AI doesn't set the granularity within a phase for you — deciding how to split the work is still your job.

scenario: 你要在 50 分钟内交付一个含 5 个同构 endpoint 的服务，得决定哪些先自己想清楚。
scenario_en: You have 50 minutes to ship a service with five identical endpoints and must decide what to think through yourself first.
q: 哪些任务更需要你先思考清楚，再让 AI 实现？（多选）
q_en: Which tasks require you to think them through first, then let the AI implement? (Select all)
options: 选择算法
生成五个同构 endpoint 的样板
处理关键边界条件
设计核心数据结构
options_en: Choosing the algorithm.
Generating boilerplate for five identical endpoints.
Handling the critical edge cases.
Designing the core data structures.
why: 算法、边界和数据结构是判断密集区；重复样板才是 AI 可以更自由处理的体量工作。
why_en: Algorithm choice, edge cases, and core data structures are judgment-heavy, while repetitive boilerplate is volume work the AI can handle with more freedom.
tradeoff: 判断密集任务（你先想清楚）vs 体量重复任务（AI 自由发挥也没关系）
optionExplanations: 算法选错会直接改变正确性和复杂度，这类判断必须你先拿主意。
五个 endpoint 结构相同，AI 复制这种模式的风险很低，可以放手。
边界条件是最容易漏、最容易出 bug 的地方，得你先想到。
数据结构一旦定下就是后续所有逻辑的地基，得你先决定。
optionExplanations_en: Picking the wrong algorithm changes correctness and complexity directly, so that call has to be yours first.
Five identical endpoints are low-risk for the AI to copy the pattern — you can let it run free here.
Edge cases are where bugs slip through most easily, so you need to spot them yourself first.
Once the data structure is set it becomes the foundation for everything downstream, so decide it yourself first.

scenario: 你正在修一个具体 bug，AI 却建议顺手重构整个类层级，你说不出这对修 bug 有什么帮助。
scenario_en: You're fixing one specific bug and the AI suggests refactoring the entire class hierarchy, with no benefit you can articulate.
q: AI 建议重构整个类层级，但你解释不出收益，最主要风险是什么？
q_en: If the AI suggests refactoring the whole class hierarchy and you cannot explain the benefit, what is the main risk?
options: 代码一定会更短
范围膨胀，时间耗在无关改动上
测试数量会自动变多
面试官一定更满意
options_en: The code is guaranteed to be shorter.
Scope creep: time gets burned on changes unrelated to the goal.
The number of tests automatically goes up.
The interviewer is guaranteed to be more satisfied.
why: 无理由的大重构会把你从计划带走，也会让后续每个生成结果更难解释和验证。
why_en: An unjustified rewrite pulls you away from the plan and makes every later output harder to explain and verify.

termDefinitions.meaning: 范围蔓延：改动不断超出原计划边界，消耗与目标无关的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep means changes keep expanding beyond the original plan and burn time on work unrelated to the goal.

optionExplanations: 代码长短跟有没有收益无关，重构后也可能反而更冗长。
时间被无根据的改动占用，题目本身要解决的目标反而完不成。
测试数量不会因为重构自动增加，得你额外补上。
面试官更可能追问收益在哪里，而不是自动就更满意。
optionExplanations_en: Code length has nothing to do with whether there's an actual payoff — a rewrite can come out longer.
Time gets burned on unjustified changes, and the actual problem you were supposed to solve stays unsolved.
Test count doesn't grow on its own from a rewrite — you'd have to add those yourself.
The interviewer is more likely to ask what the payoff is than to automatically be pleased.

scenario: 这是 Rippling 式一轮:面试官沿途一个接一个给你测试用例,你增量地把功能建出来,而不是照着预列好的 bug→feature→optimize 阶段走。
scenario_en: This is a Rippling-style round: the interviewer hands you test cases one at a time as you build features incrementally, rather than following a pre-listed bug to feature to optimize phase list.
q: 你的拆解应该怎么组织?
q_en: How should you organize your decomposition?
options: 把整份阶段计划提前锁死,先不理会陆续给的用例
按陆续给的用例推进,一次实现一个功能过掉当前用例
跳过拆分,反正测试用例会替你把一切都定义好
把手上所有用例一次性丢给 AI,让它一口气把功能全写完
options_en: Lock in the full phase plan up front and ignore the test cases as they arrive.
Build incrementally, one feature at a time, to pass the test case you just got.
Skip decomposition since the test cases will define everything for you.
Dump every test case you have into the AI at once and let it build all the features in one go.
why: Rippling 式面试的用例是沿途逐个给的,拆解要跟着用例节奏走:每来一个用例就实现一个功能过掉它;代价是你不能像 Meta 那样提前锁死全部阶段,得随新用例调整顺序。
why_en: At Rippling the interviewer feeds test cases one at a time, so you pace your decomposition to them, building one feature per incoming case rather than pre-locking every phase.
whenOtherWins: 如果是 Meta 式题面已经写死 bug→feature→optimize 三阶段,就该提前规划完整阶段顺序,而不是等用例。
tradeoff: 跟用例增量推进(随新用例调整顺序)vs 提前锁死阶段(结构清晰但不适配沿途给用例的格式)
optionExplanations: 提前锁死阶段是 Meta 式题面的做法;这轮用例是沿途给的,死守旧顺序会和新用例对不上。
面试官每给一个用例,你就实现一个功能过掉它,拆解节奏跟着用例走。
用例只说明要过什么,不替你决定实现顺序和数据结构,跳过拆分照样失控。
一次全丢给 AI,多个功能被压进一次输出,还没来得及用用例逐个验证就难追踪。
optionExplanations_en: Locking phases up front is the Meta-style move; here the cases arrive along the way, so a fixed order drifts out of sync with each new case.
Each case the interviewer gives, you implement one feature to pass it, pacing the decomposition to the cases.
A test case only says what to pass, not the order or data structures, so skipping decomposition still loses control.
Dumping them all at once buries several features in one output you can't verify case by case.

scenario: 面试中你让 AI 自己发明了一套和现有类平行的架构,没引用代码库里已有的类;面试官指着其中一个类问 what does this class do。
scenario_en: During the interview you let the AI invent its own architecture parallel to the existing classes instead of referencing them; the interviewer points at one class and asks what it does.
q: 这一问最容易暴露什么?
q_en: What does that question most easily expose?
options: 那个类一定藏着编译错误,只是测试还没跑到它
你讲不清这个类做什么,因为架构是 AI 发明的,没经你手
面试官只是随口一问,答不出也不影响这轮评估
答不上来也没关系,当场再让 AI 把这个类从头到尾重新解释一遍就行
options_en: That class must be hiding a compile error the tests just haven't reached yet.
You can't say what it does, because the AI invented the architecture, not you.
The interviewer is only making small talk, so failing to answer won't affect the round.
No problem, just have the AI explain this class from top to bottom again for you on the spot.
why: 引用已有的类是为了你能解释代码库每一处;放任 AI 发明平行架构的代价,是你和代码失联,一句 what does this class do 就当场戳穿。
why_en: You reference existing classes so you can explain the whole codebase; when the AI invents a parallel architecture, one 'what does this class do?' exposes that you can't.
optionExplanations: 编译错误跟你能不能解释职责是两回事;这一问戳的是理解,不是语法。
架构是 AI 自己发明的,关键决策没经你手,所以你说不清它到底做什么。
这不是闲聊,答不出正是面试官用来判断你有没有和代码脱节的信号。
让 AI 再解释一遍只证明你要靠它读自己的代码,反而坐实了脱节。
optionExplanations_en: A compile error is a different matter from whether you can explain the class; the question probes understanding, not syntax.
The AI invented the architecture and the key calls never passed through you, so you can't say what it does.
This isn't small talk; failing to answer is exactly the signal the interviewer uses to catch you drifting from the code.
Having the AI re-explain it only shows you rely on it to read your own code, which confirms the disconnect.

scenario: 从零构建的题,时间紧,你跳过给实体建模,直接冲去写最有意思的核心逻辑;进入后一阶段时需求变得更具体。
scenario_en: In a greenfield build under time pressure, you skip modeling the entities and jump straight to the interesting core logic; then a later phase makes the requirements more specific.
q: 这种跳步最典型的后果是什么?
q_en: What is the most typical consequence of skipping ahead like this?
options: 代码缠在没定型的模型上,后期需求一具体就难重构,被迫返工
代码早期跑得动,所以后面阶段也不会因为缺模型而翻车返工
先写有意思的逻辑其实更快,数据模型可以边写边定型,几乎不用回头
缺的数据模型 AI 会在后面阶段察觉并自动帮你补齐好
options_en: The code tangles onto an unsettled model, so when requirements get specific later, it won't refactor and you rewrite.
The code runs early on, so later phases won't break or force rework from the missing model either.
Writing the interesting logic first is actually faster, and the data model can settle as you go with almost no backtracking.
The AI will notice the missing data model in a later phase and fill it in for you automatically.
why: 先建模会逼你在写逻辑前理清对象和关系;跳过它省下眼前几分钟,代价是后一阶段需求变具体时,代码建在漂移的地基上,只能推倒返工。
why_en: Modeling first makes you understand the objects before the logic; skipping it saves minutes now but forces a rewrite when a later phase pins requirements onto a shifting foundation.
optionExplanations: 没有稳定的数据模型,AI 生成的逻辑缠在一起,需求一具体就得推倒重来。
早期能跑不代表撑得住;后一阶段需求变细,缺模型的代码正是最先崩的地方。
先写逻辑看似快,实际是把理解对象的成本推到后面,连本带利地还。
AI 不会替你决定核心模型,它只会在你没定的地基上继续叠代码。
optionExplanations_en: Without a stable data model, the AI's logic tangles together and has to be torn down once requirements get specific.
Running early doesn't mean holding up; when a later phase tightens requirements, the model-less code is the first to break.
Writing logic first looks fast but only defers the cost of understanding the objects, which you pay back with interest.
The AI won't decide the core model for you; it just keeps stacking code on the foundation you never set.
